utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, before you resume your examination-in-chief, the Judge -- you would appreciate that the Judges not being possessed of the attribute of by location are only today catching up with matters that will have come in while we were away from The Hague, and one of them which is of some urgency is your motion relating to Thursday's witness. So what we have determined is that the most efficient way time-wise of dealing with this would be if we -- if you were to suspend your examination-in-chief of the witness who is now in the box say 15 minutes early, about 1.30, and we could hear further from you on that motion and get the Defence's response and we may be able to dispose of it before we rise for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I can do that, Your Honour. I will ask my case manager to e-mail Ms. Pidwell who is going to be handling that witness to come down at 1.30 and we can address it with you then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Witness now I want to talk to you about War Commissions. Did you have an occasion in 1992 to meet a man called Dragan Djokanovic?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I understand he was a -- well, let me ask you this: You were aware about decisions at the republican level to try and create War Commissions partly to do away or decommission the previously established Crisis Staffs. Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: I heard that even before Dragan Djokanovic arrived, but that was the time when I first saw a decision to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me show you now Exhibit P398. This is a document referring to the appointment of members of a War Commission for the Serbian municipality of Zvornik, and it's dated the 17th of June. Purports to be based on review of a report submitted by Dr. Djokanovic. Have you seen this document before? I think you saw it during proofing. I don't know if you saw it in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: I believe I saw it, most probably I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you see the members include Dr. Djokanovic and number 3 is Branislav Grujic. That's Mr. Grujic who was president of the interim government. We've heard evidence that Dr. Djokanovic initially proposed a different person rather than Mr. Grujic. He proposed I think Jovan Ivanovic as the third member of the War Commission. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what happened when Mr. Grujic found out that it was being proposed that he, Mr. Grujic, not be part of this newly to-be-formed commission, how did he react?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: Dr. Dragan Djokanovic was a republican commissioner, and from the outset he had problems with the setting up of the commission. And from the outset he encountered disagreements about the goal of his arrival. That was the biggest problem. And the goal of his arrival was to disband the interim government, to restore the functioning of the Municipal Assembly in Zvornik with all of its bodies. And the way Djokanovic went about that business was something that Brano Grujic opposed to, and he also opposed the goal that he had, at least the goal as Dragan Djokanovic had envisaged it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And we see in this document that Dr. Karadzic is the one who actually confirmed the appointment that included Mr. Grujic. After this document was there any War Commission established in Zvornik municipality?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we go into private session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: One of the things that's spoken about in that document is trying to resolve the matter of the SJB chief. Do you recall who was the president of the SJB as of 1 July 1992? Was that Mr. Veselic, Marinko?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: I really can't remember who the president was, but the commission -- could I please read the second article of this decision if that's what you're still talking about; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: "Due to the specific situation, the position of Zvornik ... municipality and the lack of staff, we are unable to resolve the following matter: The SJB chief. The War Commission is requesting help from the Ministry of the Interior for the permanent solution of this staffing problem." One of the chiefs was one of the police officers who hailed from Loznica. I don't know how long he stayed in that position and for how long, and I don't know whether it was Marinko or that other guy whose family name was Pantelic or something like that. I'm not sure who it was. However, the problem was the fact that the police were unable to do their job and they couldn't do it because they were under the great influence of the commander of the Territorial Defence. They did not secure what they were supposed to secure. They were supposed to secure the population. They were supposed to look after public law and order. What they did instead, they mobilised the population and they sent them to the front line; and that was the gist of the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me show you Exhibit P341. This is tab 31 of the documents proposed for this witness. I want to show you a document now that may refresh your recollection about who was the chief on a particular date and when he was replaced by someone else. This is a MUP document dated the 2nd of August, 1992, and it indicates that the current chief as of that date was Marinko Vasilic and he was being replaced on that date by Milorad Lokancevic. Does that refresh your memory about when the change took place and who the new chief was as of 2nd of August?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: As of the 2nd of August, 1992, the chief was Lokancevic as of the 2nd of August, 1992. However, the previous document covered an earlier period. It didn't cover this particular date, did it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, correct. And my question was V asilic the chief as of July 1st?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: Vasilic stayed in the position until the moment Lokancevic was appointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know a man named Dragan Adnan who was a police inspector with the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: Yes, I did know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I would next like to show you a document that's also in evidence Exhibit P338 dated -- it's tab number 23 and I want to show you this and ask you about a couple of paragraphs in that talk about the situation in Zvornik. in regard to the SJB. I see the first page is dated the 17th of June, and if we could go to page 4 of the B/C/S and page 5 of the English. Witness, I will tell you this is a section of a report from Dragan Adnan that's talking about the public security station in Zvornik. And if you could look at the first two paragraphs -- or, I'm sorry, the second and third paragraphs on your page.

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing this during proofing?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And it talks about some of the problems in Zvornik with the paramilitary formations, some problems with Captain Dragan. And the last sentence in that first paragraph says: "Due to such a decision and legalisation of the stay by criminally inclined persons in this area, the chief of SJB Zvornik dissatisfied with the decision by military authorities has submitted a request to be released from this duty." I take it that refers to Marinko Vasilic; yes?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: I really can't remember, but I believe that it does refer to Marinko Vasilic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And that seems consistent with what you were saying before about the police or the police chief not being able to do much because of Pavlovic and how everybody was being mobilised and run by the TO?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: He had constant problems and conflicts with Pavlovic with this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the next paragraph talks about how some of these persons have committed rapes and even killed Muslim nationals who were ready for exchange. They'd surrounded the government and Crisis Staff building, and one of the members of Captain Dragan's paramilitary even threatened the president of the government, holding a pistol under his throat. Did you know about that, about those events?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: I remember that event when the building of the municipality was surrounded. We had expected people to come to go on talking about information and transition to what the commission wanted us to do. And while we were waiting for the people to gather, in the meantime the building of the Municipal Assembly had been surrendered -- had been surrounded. They focused mostly on Brano Grujic. The people were saying that he had been ill-treated, that there was a knife at his throat, that he had been threatened, but I myself did not see that. But I know that the building was surrounded and that I do know that things like that did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: 64, 25, I believe the witness said that -- what was the position that Brano Grujic was holding at that point and it wasn't recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what position Mr. Grujic held at that time?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic was the president of the interim government at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I want to show you one more document. Do you recall, pertaining to some of these issues, do you recall a meeting that took place in Zvornik on the 30th of June, 1992, which was attended by, among others, General Ratko Mladic and President Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Where was that meeting held?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: That meeting was held in the building of the Municipal Assembly of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could, I'd like to take a look at 65 ter 3583.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is -- this document is one of some of the Mladic notebooks, and I think this may be the first time that we're dealing with any of those in court. I want to show the witness a particular excerpt. I think what I'll do at the end of that, I may ask to have it marked for identification because I know there are probably still pending issues with the Defence about authenticity, et cetera, but I think you'll see why I want to use it with him. And I would like to start with page 246 in the English in e-court and I think the B/C/S page is 244. And for present purposes, if the usher could help me by handing the witness a hard copy of the B/C/S I think it will go a little quicker. And if in e-court we can have up those pages, 246 in English and 244 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Witness, the first page I have reference is Zvornik, Tuesday 30 June 1992, 1330 hours, entitled: "Meeting with representatives of Zvornik municipality." And there are a list of attendees.

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: Something is unclear here if I may say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, what did you want to say? I think -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: This is what I wanted to say, that here in the introduction it says: "Meeting with the representatives of the Zvornik Municipal Assembly," but then read the list of attendees. President of the Municipal Assembly of Bratunac and it goes on to Sekovici and then other places and all these people do not represent the Zvornik Municipal Assembly. I said to you what I remember from the meeting that I attended, but I'm not sure whether this is a summary of several meetings, that is, one summary note covering several meetings, that's one thing; and secondly, whether it's authentic at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Witness, I appreciate your volunteering to help me with the authenticity, but that's not what I want to ask you. Did you attend a meeting on the 30th of June with Dr. Karadzic and General Mladic in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Who else was at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: At that meeting there may have been 15 people. When I was there, there was Branko Grujic and I from Zvornik municipality, and there was also Captain Dragan at that meeting. And there were other people whom I don't remember now. I told you last time that I wasn't sure about Marko Pavlovic. I don't remember him saying anything at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you stay for the entire meeting that you attended or did you leave while other people were still meeting?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: I left the meeting before the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go to page 249 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And for you, Witness, I think it's the fourth page. I have highlighted Branko Grujic's name. I think you may have just passed it. On the left --

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And under him the words are written: "We have 32.000 Serbs. "We have successfully implemented the President's decision to settle Divic and Kozluk with our children." In Zvornik at that time were you resettling Serb refugees into the abandoned villages of Divic and Kozluk that the Muslims had then left?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: At that time Serb refugees that had come to Zvornik were settled in the abandoned villages -- the abandoned areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: He goes on to speak about problems with various formations and Dencic called together these groups called Zuca and similar. Captain Dragan appeared out of nowhere requesting to form a centre. That's all correct and consistent with what you saw happened in Zvornik, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: That's true. Even at that meeting the -- this problem was raised, and I mean Captain Dragan's request to establish a centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And had you in -- you -- had people in the municipal government opposed or denied that request by Captain Dragan to form a centre in Divic?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: We opposed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now if we could go to page 251 in the English and I think it's one page over for you, I see the name Marko Pavlovic highlighted on the left?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And these remarks appear to be attributed to him. If you could go over one more page, turn over one more page in your B/C/S and it's page 250 in the English. At the bottom of my page it's written as: "We were most active in evicting the Muslims. We had brought peace to Sepak, Divic, and Kozluk. Some of them wanted to move out while we demanded it." That's consistent with your experience, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but we are not getting the proper Serbian text on the monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Witness, can you tell us what number is on the bottom of your B/C/S page?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: I'm trying to find what you're referring to. Number 5 in my version is Marko Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think it's 251 in the B/C/S. It's 253 in the English in e-court. Yes, it's the bottom of that page in B/C/S on the screen: "We were most active in evicting the Muslims, we had" -- and then we have to go to the next page in e-court and B/C/S and likewise in English, we have to continue on to the next page: " ... brought peace to Sepak, Divic, and Kozluk. Some of them wanted to move out, while we demanded it." That's consistent with your experience earlier in the year with Muslims in those municipalities, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: I don't know how to comment on this. I told you what I knew about these things, whereas this differs completely. The statements are different all together. Likewise, it says down there: "We had to evict some of the people also for the sake of our 'heros' who fled from Kovacevici." But Kovacevici is a Muslim village, so I'm unclear about what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me show you another document that may help.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could look at P321, it's tab 26. And could this 65 ter be marked for identification for present purposes?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we seriously object to this document being even marked for identification. First of all, Your Honours, we don't -- this is not the Mladic diary. This is a transcript of alleged Mladic diary prepared by the Office of the Prosecutor. So I don't really see how can we admit the document which was produced in the course of this year as an exhibit, produced by the Prosecution office. That is beyond the dispute I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And -- I'm sorry. And additionally, the witness -- the witness does not recall many of the suggestions which Mr. Hannis put to him. He expressed his reserves on the contents of it. And thirdly, he even expressed his view of the authenticity of the document. Therefore, I really don't see any basis for even MFI-ing this document. We don't know what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I am inclined to agree, Mr. Zecevic, but it seems to me that for purely practical purposes, and we now see the arguments which you are in a position to make based on this witness's testimony. But inasmuch as the evidence that has been led through this witness is of contemporaneous events, for want of a better way of describing it, it seems that so as not to lose the fact that reference has already been made to this material and we aren't losing sight of the fact that the matter of authenticity still has to be determined, that there is no prejudice to the Defence in allowing the convenience of it being marked for identification at this stage. And it may very well be that as we progress the whole thing would fall away, but I don't see any prejudice. It's merely the convenience of doing it at this point. That's my thinking.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, if I may very shortly explain, Your Honours. The document which we saw which Mr. Hannis was reading from and which he showed to the witness is not the document he's referring to. He's referring to alleged Mladic diary. This document is not Mladic diary. It is an excerpt from alleged -- alleged excerpt from the alleged Mladic diary document which was prepared by the Office of the Prosecutor, Your Honours. This is not the original document. This has nothing to do with the document which we were dealing with in the course of this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Could I hear you on that narrow point, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure what my alleged learned friend is saying because I guess if his point is what I'm using is a Latin transcript of an original Cyrillic document, if that's what he's saying then his arguments go to weight not to admissibility. And at this point I'm not asking to admit it, I'm simply asking to mark it for identification - and I think you're precisely on point, Judge - for convenience and practicality because I'm hoping by the time we get to the end of this case we will persuade you that this document is what we purport it to be by the necessary standard for it to be admitted and then you'll be able to find it and find those references. But this is just the beginning of trying to deal with these materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I just respond to the answer given by Mr. Hannis. It seems to me that there are two issues relating to the eventual admission of this excerpt. One is the authenticity and that remains to be confirmed at a much later stage when we are able to see the final translation and whether at that point it can be confirmed that the handwritten notes by General Mladic correspond to the Latin transcription that the Prosecution has made and that this Latin transcription has then been correctly translated into English. That's one issue. And I think for that purpose I don't have a difficulty in admitting the excerpt on an MFI basis at this point. But I do have another issue that relates to the contents of what we have seen on the screen, because I think I was able to pick up the number of persons who Mladic allegedly had listed as taking part in this meeting. And I think I recall that I didn't see, for instance, Branko Grujic's name among the participants. So I'm just -- I'm just raising the question, are we talking about the same meeting that the witness here says that he had with, among others, Karadzic and Mladic and, on the other hand, the meeting that General Mladic has described in his notes? Are we sure that this is one and the same meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it's the Prosecution's position that it is, that there weren't many meetings on the 30th of July in Zvornik which were attended by Dr. Karadzic and General Mladic. We have some testimony in evidence already from Dragan Djokanovic about a meeting he attended with Dr. Karadzic and General Mladic. Now, you'll see Dragan Djokanovic is listed as number 15 in the attendees of this meeting, and on the second page of English, page 247 in e-court, number 18 is Marko Pavlovic. And then there's some following names without numbers, but Branko Grujic is listed there as an attendee.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Could -- excuse me, Mr. Hannis. Could we ask the Registrar to have the document back on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The first page is page 246 in e-court of the English. And that only lists the first 17 names. Mr. Grujic's name is on the next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the document may be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1608, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now if we could show the witness Exhibit P321.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Witness, as this comes up I will tell you that this is entitled Official Note about an interview. It's with Brano Grujic. It's dated the 2nd of July, 1992, by an operative of the State Security Service. And I think you had a chance to look at this during proofing. If we could go to page 3 --

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go to page 3 of the English and it's page 3 of the B/C/S as well in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You'll see in the second half of your B/C/S page a paragraph that begins: "On the 30th of June this year, the temporary Serbian government of Zvornik discussed the issues of Captain Dragan's volunteer training centre ..." et cetera. And I would like to go to the bottom of the page where it says Dr. Radovan Karadzic and General Mladic visited Zvornik on the same day, and in the presence of Captain Dragan General Mladic, among other things, said he did not give any kind of approval for the establishment of a voluntary training centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And then I think we have to go to the next page of the B/C/S, but we can continue on the same page in English. It goes on to say: "General Mladic said about Captain Dragan that he is no more than an ordinary mobster ... that he, Captain Dragan, was looting in a manner more subtle than Arkan and his men, but that he was not far behind them." Were you aware that Captain Dragan and his men as well as Arkan and his men were looting when they were in Zvornik municipality?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: There was talk about looting throughout the war. Everybody was familiar with these stories that goods were looted from shops, from supply centres, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you about the Yellow Wasps. You knew about Zuco and his group referred to as the Yellow Wasps and some of their activities in Zvornik municipality in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: Everybody in Zvornik knew about that, that they conduct searches and inspections, that they loot and kill people. Repic was the individual who was most often mentioned as the worst of them all, as the one who mistreats others, kills them, and so on. But anyway, everybody knew about the Yellow Wasps, Pivarski, Simo Chetnik, and the other paramilitary units. And I believe that I told you that Brano Grujic gave a good description of them here and he described them accurately.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In that document you're saying Brano Grujic described it accurately in that document that we've been looking at, that Official Note --

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When the Yellow Wasps were arrested, when that big roundup occurred, did you participate in that in any fashion? Did you have anything to do with that?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: My connection with that incident has to do with Goran Zugic. When he came to Zvornik to collect information he called on me and told me what his duty was and warned me not to speak about it a lot, that he was supposed to collect information. When all necessary information is collected, that a group was already being prepared at the MUP who would be able to stand up to them physically. That is, that they were better equipped and better trained than the others. Other inspectors took part in that as well, but I mostly spoke to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And was he a member of the state security?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: I don't know. I think he was with the MUP of the RS. I don't know what his position there was, but I think he was an inspector of some kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened with the provisional government in Zvornik after July 1992? I think you started to explain a little bit when there was a session of the Municipal Assembly, but could you explain to us how the provisional government eventually came to an end?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: The provisional government ceased to exist when the Municipal Assembly was established, when a president and an executive committee of the Municipal Assembly were appointed, and the Assembly started working. From that moment on, there was no more temporary government, provisional government.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately when that occurred in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: I don't know, but I believe you have a document showing when the decision was taken to open a municipal prison and that all other detention facilities shall be closed, that a president shall be elected, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't have a document in front of me, but I seem to recall that the date was 19 August; does that sound about right?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: No, no. It must have been earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And during that session you said there was a decision taken about establishing a municipal prison in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you know why that decision was taken? There had been lots of people detained in Zvornik before that date.

utterances.speaker: ST-215
utterances.text: There was an attempt to pass a decision for the ministry and the police to lean on to take action to close down all illegal facilities, and instead establishing a prison under official control of the authorities rather than controlled by paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I go into closed session for the last two minutes before we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- finish with this witness for today. Private session I meant.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And we are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Witness, we -- your testimony is of course not completed, but we are about to take the adjournment for today and as you may have gathered there are some procedural matters with which counsel and the Bench have to deal. So you would now be escorted from the courtroom, but I would remind you that having been sworn as a witness you can't have any communication whatever with counsel from either side, and moreover in such conversations as you have with persons outside of the court you cannot discuss your testimony. So I would remind you that we resume tomorrow afternoon, so we would continue your testimony at 2.15 tomorrow afternoon. So you're now excused for the day. And as I said, just give the usher time to lower the shades so that you could be escorted from the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you don't need me here or you don't need me today anymore, do you ?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Not for the rest of the day, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Pidwell, we have your motion that was filed on the 23rd, and it's fairly straightforward but if you could in speaking to it before we call on the Defence as to whether they are in a position to respond without more -- could you help us a little bit with the arithmetic in the sense that -- and it may be that I'm completely off the mark here, that the three hours that this witness will have initially had we assume would have included the usual 20 minutes for the 92 ter witness who would have given previous testimony plus for good cause the additional two hours and 40 minutes. But we are at a bit of a loss as to understand why a fraction of 20 minutes is a third of an hour and that's a third -- why -- what would have been one-ninth -- a fraction of one-ninth of his original testimony suddenly explodes into double the three hours. I mean, we are relieved that a part of your motion is that you're not asking to enlarge the time available to you, but nevertheless perhaps you could be of assistance in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I hope I can be of assistance, Your Honour. The -- this witness provided two interviews to the OTP, one in 2001 and one in 2009. The interview that was conducted in 2001 lasted -- or it was audio recorded and lasted eight hours. It was transcribed into 94 pages of English transcript. The second interview -- firstly, that interview was done -- for -- in preparation for a different trial with a different focus. This OTP team then went and re-interviewed him last year, at the beginning of last year, and that interview was video recorded because it was a suspect interview and it took -- well, from 9.30 in the morning until 6.30 at night, so nine hours with breaks in between. That has been transcribed into English and comprises 80 pages of transcript. You will see that a lot of areas were covered and a lot of evidence or topics covered in those two interviews. We have reviewed those and because of the problems that we see with, firstly, the transcription; secondly, the fact it hasn't been translated back into B/C/S language; and thirdly, the length of time it would take for this witness to re-listen to all of that because he doesn't speak English and it's only been transcribed into English, and in addition there are some personal factors which I won't go into in respect of this witness as to why he hasn't been able to listen to those. We consider we cannot fulfil the requirements of 92 ter and that was the basis for changing his mode of testimony. This issue was actually first raised by Mr. Krgovic a couple of weeks ago with Ms. Korner directly. Unfortunately, neither of them are here to confirm that, but he raised this as what he foresaw to be a problem. So the original package, 92 ter package, comprised eight -- now, Judge Delvoie must be able to assist me with my maths, but it's 16 or 17 hours' worth of interviews. And so we asked for a couple of hours in addition to the 92 ter package to review additional documents with him and go through that process. Now if he's turning into viva voce we're going to have to condense all of the information in those two interviews from 16 or 17 hours into hopefully less than six. That is an estimate. He only arrives here today and will be proofed over the next couple of days and I'm anticipating that that estimate will shrink more, but I won't be able to provide confirmation of that until I've actually gone through the documents and his evidence with him in proofing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Pidwell, could I just ask if the problem relating to the two statements given by the witness to the Prosecution is that the recordings have not been translated into B/C/S? Is that the real problem?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: That is a large part of the real problem in terms of his reviewing the interviews because he is -- has been unable to review them with the audio files that have been provided to him. If Your Honours want to know the personal reasons for that which are personal to the witness, I can do that in private session, but he has been unable to review them to date. So we only have the audio recording in B/C/S. We have the written version in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And as I understand it part of the audio recordings are inaudible, and thus not in the transcripts?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: That's correct. Part of the transcripts have the words "inaudible" in them because the person who was transcribing them couldn't listen to the recording properly or there was background noise or there were overlapping speakers, any number of reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Is the Defence in a position to respond to this --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We do not object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, we also take no position. Obviously, it's for the Trial Chamber to decide. But just to clarify, Your Honours, my understanding is that this witness was initially provided to testify on the basis of 92 ter rule. Now you're asking to have him in viva voce. Another fact is that he didn't give any official statement to the Office of the Prosecution, also he didn't testify before the Trial Chamber in any proceedings. So we don't have any substantial condition to consider him as a 92 ter witness, we don't have any substantial documents to form his -- that's why my understanding is that our learned friend from the OTP actually shifted him from 92 ter to viva voce. There -- conditions are not fulfilled for him to be 92 ter, in short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Because -- if I may ask you, because the audio recordings have not been typed out in B/C/S; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Also he cannot review, point number one; point number two, it is not a formal written statement signed by the witness; and he didn't testify in the other proceedings before the Tribunal. So that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will grant the motion as prayed, with the clear understanding - and I can't imagine what language I can choose to make it -- well, abundantly, pellucidly, whatever word is the highest level of description, to make it clear that the time -- the extended time must be compensated for by the Prosecution in terms of some other witness. The total time that the Prosecution has remaining will not be enlarged as a consequence of the granting of this application. Yes, Mr. Pantelic, you have something?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If we have just two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If I may. Ms. Pidwell mentioned in explanation of the short history with this witness that he was -- he gave certain statements, et cetera. And she mentioned that this particular witness was interviewed in his capacity of suspect person. Unfortunately, we as a Defence we came to the conclusion, and we found many examples specifically in the year 2009 and year 2010 where our friends from the Office of the Prosecution interviewed a number of witnesses, informed them at the beginning that they are going to give the statement or interview in the capacity of suspect. My understanding is that in accordance with the Resolution of Security Council of UN, all further investigations by this Office of the Prosecution should be suspended so there is not any right for them to sort of put the pressure on the witnesses that they are a suspect. They are, number one, witnesses; number two, they are allowed to inform this witness that his statement or interview may be used in other courts, but he is not suspect. That's the point because they don't have a right and they don't have capacity to consider witness as a suspect. That's just for the record, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pantelic. I think we have been through this several times before and the Chamber has accepted the Prosecution's explanation that the reason why they would wish to interview a witness under the Rules of suspect interviews is that, exactly as you point out yourself, the witness might subsequently be a subject of prosecution before other courts. And out of an abundance of caution and in order not to trick or to lure the witness into giving information that might subsequently incriminate him before other tribunals, the Prosecution has taken the view that they should then interview him as a suspect and we have accepted that. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So we take the adjournment to 2.15 tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of September, 2010, at 2.15 p.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
